A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same benchmark-signature research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and can be matched despite reformatting and added material.

before.justification: V3 reports original results from 32 models and 88 benchmarks, including overlap analyses, leave-one-out prediction errors and token/chunk/document comparisons.

after.justification: V4 retains original empirical analyses, expands to 89 benchmarks, and reports additional generalization, robustness, statistical and qualitative results.

M1.justification: The proposed pipeline retains contextual token perplexities, Thrush screening, AIC forward selection and normalized signature correlations. Algorithm 1's added 30-segment context explanation was already documented in v3's appendices. Alternative estimators are evaluated as ablations rather than adopted as a changed method.

E1.justification: V4 adds AbsenceBench's missing-information task across numerical, poetry and GitHub material, evidenced by Figure 1's new tell_missing row and Appendix A.5.5. Appendix A.7.3 also evaluates Dolma as an alternative signature-source corpus. Existing benchmark coverage is retained.

E2.justification: V3 mentions Lasso and Elastic Net as possible regressors; v4 actually compares them with AIC and a random-feature baseline. Appendix A.7.2 also compares Thrush screening against Spearman correlation and mutual information, substantially expanding evaluated alternatives for both pipeline stages.

E3.justification: V4 adds separate held-out-model and cross-task prediction protocols, preselection-ratio sweeps from 10^-6 to 1, and corpus-size sweeps from 100K to 10B tokens. It also adds adjusted R-squared to the granularity comparison and a signature/function semantic-similarity evaluation. These extend evaluation design without replacing the original extraction settings.

E4.justification: Beyond v3's LOOCV and granularity comparison, v4 tests unseen-model generalization, task specificity versus shared confounds, alternative regularizers and screening methods, corpus dependence, threshold sensitivity and scale stability. Section 5 and Appendix A.9 additionally examine signature meaning through semantic comparisons and concrete textual examples.

E5.justification: Appendix A.6 adds 10,000-bootstrap significance tests for within-category versus cross-category overlaps, with p-values in Table 5 and stars in Figure 4. V4 also first reports ± quantities for prediction errors. Their statistical meaning is unspecified, and additional repeated runs are not established; v3's semantic bootstrapping and Mann–Whitney tests remain.

E6.justification: V4 adds substantial generalization, robustness and qualitative results, including RedPajama–Dolma matrix agreement of 0.895 and adjusted R-squared entries in Table 1. Figure 1 retains existing pairwise values but adds AbsenceBench; the reported cross-function mean changes from 0.087 to 0.105 under expanded coverage. LOOCV reporting changes from 0.075/0.180 to 0.076/0.181 for method/mean baseline, with v4 explicitly specifying 27 BBH tasks rather than establishing a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: Appendix A.7.4 adds an asymptotic argument that downstream regression scales as O(m d'^2), using dimensionality reduction to justify filtering. The signature definitions, correlation equations, sparsity assumption and SIS conditions remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The original three contributions remain. V4's abstract adds a claim about signature semantics differing from human conceptual organization and qualifies coding's isolation through its relationship with missing-information detection. It also replaces v3's multilingual/cultural characterization with culture- and humanities-oriented benchmarks.

C2.justification: New Section 5 distinguishes predictive signatures from semantic resemblance and proposes explanations involving auxiliary skills, proxy cues and statistical co-occurrence. The appendices interpret task specificity and corpus stability, acknowledge computational limits and corpus-representativeness requirements, and discuss smaller-scale applicability. The conclusion adds qualifications concerning open-ended scoring and causal understanding.

D1.justification: V4 newly links a reported code/data release and supplies explicit benchmark-labeling rules, alternative-regression hyperparameters, robustness-test settings and computational timings. Appendix A.8 reports approximately two hours per model for perplexity extraction and 30–40 minutes per benchmark for filtering/regression. The original hardware, context construction and core preprocessing details were already present in v3.

R1.justification: V4 adds citations including AbsenceBench, Dolma, Humanity's Last Exam, LESS and semantic-representation studies. It briefly positions signatures against benchmark saturation and connects interpretations to representation research, while retaining the existing related-work organization and central positioning.

P1.justification: V4 rewrites the abstract and final remarks, makes localized explanatory edits, relocates LOOCV to the robustness appendix and reorganizes appendices A–E as A.1–A.5 before adding new sections. Most existing introduction, method and results prose remains closely matched; the added scientific content does not constitute wholesale rewriting.

P2.justification: The ICLR format substantially reflows the document: Figure 1 moves onto the opening page, Figure 4 shares a page with discussion, Figure 5 has surrounding text, and previously separate algorithm/table pages are consolidated. Figure 1 gains a task row, Figure 4 gains significance annotations, Table 1 gains an adjusted R-squared column, and new statistical and sensitivity tables appear.

improvement.justification: V4 substantially addresses v3's limited validation of generalization and dependence on construction choices. Held-out-model checks, alternative-estimator comparisons, Dolma agreement of 0.895 and threshold/scale analyses directly strengthen the empirical basis for signature robustness. Concrete examples and the code/data link improve interpretability and reproducibility. Undefined ± quantities and the unexplained 27-model training subset limit some conclusions, but do not outweigh these substantial gains.
